the_priority_sweep.why: Mixed obligation/latitude is the DOMINANT defect class in this project, with five prior occurrences. A single unit very often contains BOTH an obligation AND a grant of processor latitude and gets classified by whichever half is more memorable. The rule is symmetric and bidirectional. Clause 12 is unusually dense with 'processor dependent' appearing in the same paragraph as 'shall', so a missed split was the most likely defect in this packet - and an EMPTY split list across 36 units of I/O text would itself have been suspicious.
the_priority_sweep.reviewer_verdict: All ten claimed splits are genuinely present in the source and were actually recorded. The reviewer swept every other unit in scope for a MISSED split in the opposite direction and found none.

reviewer_answers_to_posed_questions.mixed_sweep_both_directions: All claimed splits present and recorded; no missed split found.
reviewer_answers_to_posed_questions.zero_unresolved_justified: Yes. Verified rather than accepted - every unit is genuinely classifiable, none forced into a category to avoid an unresolved entry.

no_portable_oracle_claims: Processor-dependent mappings, names, actions, lengths, representations and control characters; nonphysical records; the absence of a length for an endfile record; preconnected PRINT and file identity; optional stream end markers; unbounded stream length; and cross-image identity. Each was audited in both directions by the reviewer.
